title: [PSIRT][Medium] Issues found on 'eslint' version 8.57.1
description:
Issues reported on `eslint` version 8.57.1.  
Will need to upgrade to one of the versions which has the fix: 20.20.0, 22.22.0, 24.13.0, or 25.3.0

| ID | Package | Path | Version | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2025-50537 | eslint | shiny-server/node_modules/eslint | 8.57.1 | fixed in 9.26.0 |


Ref: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/ee730f81ad53bdb8b8b476019957be11dedc988b/npm-shrinkwrap.json#L975
`npm-shrinkwrap.json` is always forcing this version to be installed. So this needs update.

title: user:aoza0za@hotmail.com
Is it necessary to install the shiny package before installing shiny-server?
description:
According to the requirements of the official website, before installing shiny-server, you need to install the shiny package first. Today, when I upgraded the shiny-server on the Linux server, I was also required to install a bunch of R packages. But in fact, my shiny app has already installed all the necessary R packages with renv, including shiny.

Not installing shiny package seems to only affect index.html and sample-apps, but does not affect users' deployment to the shiny app project

+ systemctl --system daemon-reload
+ [ -n  ]
+ _dh_action=start
+ deb-systemd-invoke start shiny-server.service
```

##  /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf

```
# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}
```

## shiny-server version

```bash
shiny-server --version
#Shiny Server v1.5.20.0
#Node.js v20.19.2
```

So, why `/var/lib/shiny-server/` instead of the usual `/srv/shiny-server/`

title: Shiny Server fail to start APPs, R and Python, prompting no such file or directory.
description:
My installation is shiny-server-1.5.20.1002-x86_64.rpm( or a previous version) on an old CentOS 7.6 machine with R 4.1.2 abd Python 3.9.7 for my personal website, and it has been working fine for a long time, but I suddenly find that it doesn't work anymore for both R and Python APPs.

The APPs are O.K.  in Rstudio Server IDE, both R & Python.

I export Shiny Server through a Nginx reverse proxy, and access the hello APP with the URL https://jeanye.cn/shiny/sample-apps/hello/

An error has occurred
The application failed to start.

The application exited during initialization.

title: Security Vulnerabilities in Shiny Open Source components
description:
Some of the Open Source components used in Shiny have security vulnerabilities or concerns:

**showdown.js**
•	showdown.js has an open security vulnerability that was discovered in 2024 in the current version and has yet to be remediated by the developer. No code updates in the past 3 years. While the CVE is only a medium risk, it is concerning about support available should a more significant vulnerability be discovered.
https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2024-1899
CVE-2024-1899 — Denial of Service Vulnerability

**bootstrap-accessibility-plugin**
•	There is on open security issue with this plugin for its use of an outdated jQuery version. https://github.com/paypal/bootstrap-accessibility-plugin/issues/122 and the code base has not been updated since 2018, so a fix is highly unlikely.

How are these security vulnerabilities addressed within Shiny?

Also, something my company's security team raised - they have a requirement that all Open Source components “Must be maintained at latest version.”  Are the OS components updated to the most recent version?

title: How to choose the python path for Shiny-Server.conf
description:
Hello, i am configuring shiny-server.conf for deploying my app on web.

Following the instructions:

> Configure Python
> 
> Next, you need to tell Shiny Server how to find Python. You can point Shiny Server at either a Python binary (e.g. /usr/bin/python3) or an absolute path to a virtualenv (e.g. /srv/shiny-server/python39-venv). You can also provide a relative path to a virtualenv (e.g. .venv) in which case, SSOS will look for that directory relative to app.py. (Don’t forget that you need to [pip install shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/py/docs/install.html) and any other Python packages needed by your app(s), into whichever Python installation or virtualenv(s) you intend to use.)
> 
> Edit the file /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf (root privileges are required). Add a line with python <path-to-python-or-venv>; to the top of the file, leaving the rest of the file alone (at least for now). For example, if you wanted to use /usr/bin/python3, the end result might look like this:

```
# Use system python3 to run Shiny apps
python /usr/bin/python3;

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}
```

I installed anaconda and the path for my interpreter is `/home/user_name/anaconda3/bin/python`. So i replaced
`usr/bin/python3;`
with
`/home/user_name/anaconda3/bin/python`.

But the web app cannot be opened with the log showing:
`/home/lin/anaconda3/bin/python: permission denied`

How can I fix this issue? Looking forward to your help!

title: Cannot use relative path for site_dir parameter in shiny-server.conf
description:
## my setup

I am using `shiny-server` with a config file located at the base of my repository (`./shiny-server.conf`). Installed through the Arch Linux AUR.

Like this: `$ shiny-server shiny-server.conf`.

I have put my app under `./shiny-app/apps/hello` such that the dir structure is now:

```
./shiny-app/apps/hello/
├── filtered_samples.csv
├── norm_count_mtx.csv
├── results.csv
├── server.R
└── ui.R
```

My `shiny-server.conf` looks like this:

```conf
run_as alex;

server {
  listen 8888;

  location / {
    site_dir ./shiny-app/apps;
    log_dir ./shiny-app/logs;
    bookmark_state_dir ./shiny-app/bookmarks;

    directory_index on;
  }
}
```

## the problem

While shiny-server seems to be able to handle `log_dir` and `bookmark_state_dir` being relative, it logs the following once I visit `localhost:8888/hello/` (it logs it inside the `log_dir`):

```
Error in `shinyAppDir()`:
! No Shiny application exists at the path "shiny-app/apps/hello"
Backtrace:
    ▆
 1. └─shiny::runApp(Sys.getenv("SHINY_APP"), port = port, launch.browser = FALSE)
 2.   ├─shiny::as.shiny.appobj(appDir)
 3.   └─shiny:::as.shiny.appobj.character(appDir)
 4.     └─shiny::shinyAppDir(x)
 5.       └─rlang::abort(...)
Ausführung angehalten (this is German for "stopped execution")
```

**HOWEVER,** once I replace site_dir with the absolute path, i.e. `/home/alex/repos/my_repo/shiny-app/apps`, it can find the app just fine.

In other words, the line now looks like this:

```
    ...

title: Request: Docs on providing environmental variables to shiny-server
description:
I'm trying to run shiny-server within a docker container. For example:

```bash
docker run -it --rm -u shiny \
  -p 5000:5000 \
  --env-file ~/.Renviron \
  ${IMG_NAME}:${IMG_VERSION}
```

However, it appears that shiny-server wipes most environmental variables, according to this [old thread](https://community.rstudio.com/t/how-to-access-os-environment-variable-from-shiny-apps-server-r/23822/3). https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/8d94d5d2543de5c33839354ae66facf07605b8e9/python/SockJSAdapter.py#L93-L105

This style of Google Analytics supports "Universal Analytics" which is Google's very old analytics platform. You can identify it by the string `UA-` that prepends the ID (the current documentation also gives an example of using a `US-` ID). However, Universal Analytics is being removed on July 1 2023 and will no longer be supported. Google Analytics 4 uses different javascript code and must be used for all web pages after July 1 2023.

title: Sending huge data through custom message Error
description:
# Context

A shiny application I work on sends processed data through:

`session$sendCustomMessage("handler", data)`

The Javascript on the front end catches this message and does some visualizations:

`Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('handler', (data) => visualizer(data))`

When the `fetch data` button is clicked this data is sent.

The shiny server is currently hosted on an Amazon EC2 R6a Large instance. 

# Issue

Depending on the parameters the user selects, the data can be small or huge. When the parameters are such that the data is a huge JSON object, there is an error given and the server disconnects with the following messages:

[![enter image description here][1]][1] 

[![enter image description here][2]][2]

I have tested the same scenarios but without sending the data through `session$sendCustomMessage("handler", data)` and am not able to reproduce the error. It seems like sending a huge amount of data through the network causes the shiny server to disconnect.

This error does not occur locally with the same parameters in RStudio and only happens on the shiny server ec2 environment.

What could be the fix for this?

  [1]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/EVPHN.png
  [2]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/61eIu.png

title: Add support for quarto
description:
Add explicit support for quarto, so that serving quarto's `.qmd` documents is equivalent to serving Rmarkdown's `.Rmd` files.

shiny-server supports a kind of render-on-demand feature for rmarkdown using `rmarkdown::run()`. We need equivalent functionality for quarto.

For anyone else reading this, it's already possible to publish _rendered_ quarto-generated html to shiny-server. This request is solely about the render-on-demand feature.

title: RobustSockJS connectivity issues caused by high client execution latency
description:
Using the attached demo app:

[client-hang.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/files/8535073/client-hang.zip)

Load it into SSOS or SSP, with `reconnect on;`. Use Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A in the browser to turn off all transports except xhr-polling, then reload.

Causing the app to hang for 10 seconds results in "RobustSockJS collision" messages. Hanging for 48 seconds results in "Discard position id too big" messages, and disconnection.

This demonstrates that SockJS, and by extension we, are not robust to the client's main thread being blocked for many seconds at a time. This in and of itself might not be that big of a problem, since we need to give up on the client at *some* point; but it's a problem right now because it's not at all clear to the app author or admin what they're doing wrong.

title: Apps using reticulate don't exit on shiny-server stop/restart
description:
Install the following app under a subdirectory of `/srv/shiny-server/`:

#### app.R
```r
library(shiny)

reticulate::source_python("test.py")

ui <- "Hello"

server <- function(input, output, session) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

#### test.py
```python
print(1)
```

## Prerequisites

Your run_as user needs the reticulate R package installed, and a reticulate-compatible python environment (running `reticulate::install_miniconda()` is what I did).

## Repro instructions

1. Run `pgrep R` before launching Shiny Server, hopefully there are no processes but if there are take note of them.
2. Launch Shiny Server.
3. Load the above app.
4. Do `pgrep R` again, see the new pid that has appeared.
5. Without closing the browser, stop Shiny Server.
6. Do `pgrep R` again, see that the new pid has not disappeared; i.e., the R process has leaked!

## Explanation

This happens because Shiny Server's normal strategy for stopping R processes is by sending `SIGINT`, waiting 20 seconds, and sending `SIGTERM` if necessary. This works fine when the server is running normally. But during shutdown, `SIGINT` is sent but there isn't time for 20 seconds to pass to follow up with `SIGTERM` if necessary. In this case, something about using reticulate/python causes `SIGINT` signals to be ignored by the R process; but `SIGTERM` would have worked.

The fix is that when shiny-server is shutting down, it should be less polite and just send `SIGTERM`. (Note that there's no real-world evidence that `SIGTERM` is worse for Shiny apps than `SIGINT`, when I wrote this code many years ago it just seemed the right thing to do to simulate a user hitting Ctrl+C, so any tryCatch/finally could run--but RStudio Connect just sends `SIGTERM` and it doesn't seem to have been a problem for anyone.)

title: Security issue: inline script preventing secure CSP: preShinyInit
description:
My organization requires strict content security policy, including no inline styles or javascript. Hashes can be added to allow an exact inline script to run, but if that script changes these hashes will require updates and this could bring down multiple apps after an update, potentially. 

shiny-server seems to only use inline scripts in one place: shiny-server\R\SockJSAdapter.R ~line 194 `sprintf("preShinyInit({reconnect:%s,disableProtocols:[%s]});"...`

If this could be moved to a JS file that would make it easier to build sites that follow strict CSP.

title: Unclear how to change temp dir for shiny-server
description:
Currently shiny-server creates tempdirs in `/tmp` and it is unclear how to change this:

* It is not a config option (AFAIK based on the documentation)
* The only time `/tmp` is in the documentation is at the bottom of https://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#running-shiny-server-with-root-privileges, there it says 
    > Finally, if the directory /tmp/shiny-server/ exists, it (and all files within it) should be owned by the user you specify.
  
  However, this directory (even if I create it) is not used by shiny-server
* So my next thought was setting an environment variable, so I used the instructions at https://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#environment-variable-settings to set `TMPDIR=/tmp/shiny-server`, but shiny-server ignores this
* After some googling, creating an `.Renviron` in my shiny app with `TMPDIR` successfully changed the temp dir for that app only
* So finally, by creating `/home/shiny/.Renviron` I was able to fix the temp dir for all apps on shiny-server

Can this be made more clear in the documentation? (and maybe the tmpdir should be a configuration option? (I am using it on our server to give shiny app authors read access to this tmpdir by setting the `setgid` bit on that directory))

---
**PS** Regarding https://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#environment-variable-settings, the recommended way of changing these systemd files is with 
```bash
systemctl edit shiny-server.service
```
this will leave the (shiny-server package maintained) `/etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service` untouched, but creates override conf files in `/etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service.d/` (see https://serverfault.com/a/840999).

title: Avoid browser timeouts for slow initializing apps
description:
This is the same as https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2967 but I think it's more appropriate here on shiny-server:

If I do long calculations in global.R my chrome browser runs into [a hard 30 second timeout](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39751124/increase-timeout-limit-in-google-chrome) because shiny-server does not respond.
Some time after chrome disconnects shiny-server will stop the (still initializing) app because it runs into ``app_idle_timeout``. Next time I try to access the page it starts from the beginning and runs into a timeout again. The app appears to be not working.

There are various workarounds for this problem:

## The progressive lazy
[Lazy load the data (in server.R) and show a progress bar](http://www.mazsoft.com/blog/post/2018/01/01/show-progress-bar-when-pre-loading-data-in-shiny-app).
This is inconvenient to develop though. And the user still has to wait.

## The fast
Cache the data somewhere and let the app load the data from cache.
But you have to maintain the cache and that is always a hard problem.

## The manual
Increase ``app_idle_timeout`` to make sure your app has enough time to start. Then just click reload in your browser after some minutes. It will connect to the now running app. 
However, if you wait too long, shiny will kill the app after ``app_idle_timeout``.

## The ugly 
Create an html page, that contains an iframe pointing to your app. After n seconds (typical start time < n <  ``app_idle_timeout``)  forward the browser to the real app using a meta refresh tag. 
That way, if the browser is left alone, it will eventually open the app and keep it running.

## The default <- This is the feature request
If an app is initializing and the browser has been waiting for more than 20s, create an info page that shows "app initializing since 123s" and refresh this page every 20s. 
Show an error if initializing takes longer than ``app_init_timeout``
Probably the 20s wait should be configurable. 

This solution would work reasonably out of the box. If you want it fast, you got to cache.

title: Start R Process on Shiny Server Startup
description:
Hello, 

I am using shiny server Open Source (https://hub.docker.com/r/rocker/shiny) and I am deploying the app via Kubernetes/Docker. My app begins by pulling RDS files from an S3 object store so initialization of the app takes about 30 seconds, however the objects are stored globally so they are shared between sessions. However, it seems that my R app doesn't initialize until the first time someone hits the app rather than when I push the app and shiny server starts. Can this be changed so the app starts up immediately when shiny server starts rather than when the first user attempts to hit the app? 

With the current setup the first user would need to wait ~30 seconds for the app to load and if I increase the number of replicas then this would conceivably happen to the same number of users.

Thank you very much

title: [Low pri] Reconnecting CSS causes really awkward flickering
description:
When an app loses connection, a few attempts to reconnect are made by the server.

This css https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/4b588a12f844713729991d1274764d854d90a18d/assets/shiny-server.css#L1-L4 removed the background of the body tag when a reconnection is attmpted. The result is that if there is already a background on the body, for a few seconds the backgroud is removed which looks glitchy.

Here's an example (the time is not to scale, converting video to GIF messed up the timing)

![2020-06-09-02-30-36](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/952340/84114023-9d589300-a9f9-11ea-89fb-e15958b2428a.gif)


The only way around this seems to have to define a shiny app's css with

```
body {
  background: #fafafa !important;
}
```

And it seems a bit overkill to have to use `important` because of this. Is that background clearing really required?

title: Shiny Server Pro source
description:
It is my understanding that Shiny Server Pro is a derivative work of Shiny Server, including contributions made to this repository under the AGPL3. Unless copyright was reassigned by those contributors (of which I found no evidence) those contributions are covered by AGPL3 as stated in section 5, point c of the license (emphasis added):

> c) You must license the entire work, as a whole, under this License to anyone who comes into possession of a copy. This License will therefore apply, along with any applicable section 7 additional terms, to the whole of the work, and all its parts, regardless of how they are packaged. **This License gives no permission to license the work in any other way, but it does not invalidate such permission if you have separately received it.**

Now I have downloaded the evaluation version of Shiny Server Pro, which as established above is covered under the AGPL3 and no other license if it incorporates contributions without copyright reassignment. Section 6 of the license states:

> You may convey a covered work in object code form under the terms of sections 4 and 5, provided that you also convey the machine-readable Corresponding Source under the terms of this License, in one of these ways:
>
> - a) [...] a physical product [...], accompanied by the Corresponding Source [...]
> - b) [...] a physical product [...] accompanied by a written offer [...] to give anyone who possesses the object code either (1) a copy of the Corresponding Source [...] on a durable physical medium [...] or (2) access to copy the Corresponding Source from a network server at no charge.
> - c) [...] from a designated place (gratis or for a charge), with a copy of the written offer to provide the Corresponding Source. [...]
> - d) [...] from a designated place (gratis or for a charge), and offer equivalent access to the Corresponding Source in the same way through the same place at no further charge. [...]
> - e) [...] using peer-to-peer transmission, provided you inform other peers where the object code and Corresponding Source of the work are being offered to the general public at no charge under subsection 6d.

Points (c) and (d) apply, given that the trial was distributed from an online source. However, I found no written offer for the source code (c) or a download link (d).

Please either a) inform me where I can find the source, or b) assert that the Shiny Server Pro includes no contributions that are covered under the AGPL3 license.

Note that the source code would necessarily include any additional components of the derived work as the license provides no linking exception.

title: Simplify disable_protocols options
description: The `disable_protocols` directive requires you to specify each individual protocol you want to blacklist; this precision is rarely useful, it's far more likely to want to disable "all streaming" or "all polling"; it's hard to even know which options are streaming and which are polling (not all have streaming/polling in their names). title: Permit allow-listing environment variables to be passed to R processes
description:
In cloud environments, it's common to use environment variables to pass secrets and other configuration information to otherwise static apps (containers, and similar). ShinyServer currently filters out these envvars. Solutions such as https://twitter.com/ellisvalentiner/status/1175163382401515522 involve modifying the shiny-server.sh script to pipe env variables into Renviron. That's a work around, but it makes the variables static (changes in env variables are not picked up even through app restarts) and requires maintaining custom scripts.

Requesting an allowlist system to allow envvars matching a regex (by name) be passed along to the R session.

Thanks for the consideration!

title: Different session$onSessionEnded behavior in shinyServer vs shiny from Rstudio?
description:
I posted a question about shiny server to Rstudio community yesterday (https://community.rstudio.com/t/app-feature-works-on-shinyapps-io-but-not-with-shiny-server-pro/36285). I thought a cross-post might be useful in case you don't see that post.

I have an application running on shinyapps.io (https://vnijs.shinyapps.io/radiant-data). Works great. It also works as expected from Rstudio on macOS, Windows, Linux, and Rstudio Cloud. However, when I run it on a linux (Ubuntu 18.04) server with shiny-server (1.5.9.923) or shiny-server pro (1.5.11.994) one specific feature does not work.

If you go to the app url shown above and too, for example, the View tab and select a single variable, the variable and tab selection should be correctly shown again after a browser refresh (i.e., app state is maintained). See screenshot below for an illustration. This uses `onSessionEnded` to save state information and load it back in on refresh.

Again, this feature works as expected everywhere except shiny-server and shiny-server pro. Note: There are no browser or server errors shown that could provide a clue as to why this one feature does not work.

Do you have any idea about the setup (OS) and configuration (shiny-server.conf) used for the shinyapps.io server that might cause this difference? I have not other idea about why this might be happening at this stage.

If you would like to replicate the issue you can run the app with docker and shiny-server on Ubuntu 18.04 using the command below:

docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -p 8787:8787 vnijs/radiant

You can then view the app at the following url: http://localhost:8080. The feature does work from rstudio at http://localhost:8787 by running radiant::radiant()

I just noticed that when running from shiny server the app does still state a state-file with current settings that it is supposed to loaded back in during the refresh. However, for some reason this takes about 20sec with shiny-server and by that time the browser has already completed its refresh and ignores the file. Again, with the same data and settings this works great when run from Rstudio or on shinypapps.io. From Rstudio it even works with big-ish datasets of > 700MB

title: CSS and JS files return 400 when request has Content-Length: 0
description:
In the beginning, Shiny Server was deployed on our internal container-as-a-service platform without any dramas. Life was good.

Then one of the platform teams put a reverse proxy in front of my container, and things broke. HTML was coming through just fine, but requests for the CSS and JS files were giving 400s. Not good.

The platform team did a whole bunch of investigation, and found a minimum reproducible example: if you add `Content-Length: 0` to the header of the request, you get a 400. If you remove `Content-Length: 0`, it works. The team is confident that adding `Content-Length: 0` is acceptable within the relevant standards, which makes it a bug with how Shiny Server handles the requests. They're happy to provide some tcp dumps if that's helpful.

There is a pretty easy workaround for me: I'm turning the proxy off. But we got into a discussion about R vs Python so I'm really hoping you can fix this bug so that I can point to this as an example of "look how good/strong the R open source community is!" But it's not critical for me, and probably shouldn't be high priority unless it's impacting others too.

And thanks for making such an awesome tool!

title: Redirect should optionally preserve path info
description:
The `redirect` directive currently throws away path information and redirects to the exact URL you specify. This isn't helpful if you're trying to redirect to a new location for the application (as opposed to a "Site is down" kind of page). We could add a new argument to the directive that allows preserving of path info/query string.

Here's the part of the code that would need to be enhanced to preserve the path.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/4b588a12f844713729991d1274764d854d90a18d/lib/router/router.js#L309-L333

title: error message from grep during deb postinst.in
description:
Hi,
I noticed during installation inside docker image error:
`grep: /etc/init/shiny-server.conf: no such file or directory`

I guess it's output of:
```
else
   cp ${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/shiny-server/config/init.d/debian/shiny-server /etc/init.d/

   if ! grep -e "^export LANG=" /etc/init/shiny-server.conf > /dev/null; then
      echo "Adding LANG to /etc/init.d/shiny-server, setting to $SS_LANG"
      sed -i "10 a export LANG='$SS_LANG'" /etc/init.d/shiny-server
fi
```
from https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/packaging/debian-control/postinst.in
INIT_SYSTEM is equal to entrypoint script, in my case init.sh.
I don't want to challenge logic of the conditional, but I think it can be made in more expressive way, that will not show this error message.

title: Disconnect from Server - Reuse of existing instance - still killed
description:
Dear shiny-server team,

first of all: Great work and great product!
Still, I'm experiencing some problems regarding disconnections with my (open source) version of shiny server. As far as I can tell from the log (please find it attached), my app starts normally and creates a worker. If I close the connection (e.g. close the browser), the worker remains active for some time. When I reconnect, then I get reassigned to the still running worker. So far so good. But for some reason, although reusing the existing instance, shiny-server says that there is no client connected and closes the connections. Thus, I get a greyed-out screen in my browser with a "disconnected from server" message.
I'm pretty sure, that this is not the intended behaviour and thus a issue. Yet, if it should be the intended behaviour, is there a way to avoid getting disconnected?

Thanks in advance and sorry, if the question shows my lack of knowledge...still beginning. 


[Background: I will have classes working with the app and I'm sure some may "misbehave" and click on the reload button, close the browser and reopen it,...]


[shiny-server-log.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/files/2589939/shiny-server-log.txt)

title: Failing to Start on RHEL 7
description:
Hi shiny-server and Linux gurus!

Just installed `shiny-server-1.5.9.923-x86_64` on a new RHEL 7 machine, but I can't see the test page :/

Following installation, I opened port 80 with: 
```
firewall-cmd --permanent  --zone=public --add-port=80/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```
which has apparently worked: 
```
 sudo iptables-save | grep 80
-A IN_public_allow -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
```
here's the output for `netstat`, seems like it's' not listening to port 80,
```
sudo  netstat -lnp
Active Internet connections (only servers)

tcp        0      0 127.0.0.1:631           0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      1125/cupsd
udp        0      0 127.0.0.1:323           0.0.0.0:*                           779/chronyd
```

And the status command:

```
sudo systemctl status shiny-server

 shiny-server.service - ShinyServer
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service; enabled; vendor preset: disabled)
   Active: inactive (dead) since Thu 2018-10-18 14:52:19 PDT; 23min ago
  Process: 19655 ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/env sleep 5 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
  Process: 19642 ExecStart=/usr/bin/env bash -c exec /opt/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
Main PID: 19642 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)

Oct 18 14:52:13 ipress systemd[1]: Started ShinyServer.
Oct 18 14:52:13 ipress systemd[1]: Starting ShinyServer...
```
here's `shiny-server.conf`:
```
# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
#  listen 3838;
  listen 80;
  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }

}

```
Disabling `firewalld` did not work. 
There are no files in `/var/log/shiny-server`.

I can ping the server from other machines.

title: Add active-users to Health-Check
description:
I'm currently monitoring the health-check-endpoint with the suggested health-check-json template. http://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#health-check-endpoint and it works like a charm:
/etc/shiny-server/health-check-json:
```
{ "activeConnections": #active-connections#,
  "activeApps": #active-apps#,
  "activeProcesses": #active-processes#
}
```
However, as I'm resticted by the amount of concurrent users on the server due to licenses; this is the measure I really want to see here. But simply adding `#active-users#` did not cut it... 

My goal is to quantize how often we are hitting the limit and thus pushing for additional licenses.

title: C stack usage error
description:
I have a shiny app under development that is designed to run continuously on an Amazon Lightsail instance with 1 core and 4G memory. It's at [dev.open-meta.org/app](http://dev.open-meta.org/app/).

The app has never crashed while I'm using it, but it has now crashed several times while I'm not using it, always with a C stack usage error. The most recent crash is quite interesting, here's the message:

```
Error: C stack usage  1031500945536 is too close to the limit
Execution halted
```
How can I have a [1031 Gig C Stack](https://www.google.com/search?q=1031500945536+bytes+in+gigabytes&oq=1031500945536+bytes+in+gigabytes&aqs=chrome..69i57j6.9300j0j7&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8) on an instance with only 4 Gigs of memory?

Google searches suggest the C stack usage error is usually caused by out-of-control recursion. I don't have anything like that in my code.

Is this a Shiny-Server, R, or Linux error? Do you have any further ideas for debugging what's happening?

title: Subdirectory name that includes file extension .Rmd is confused for filename
description:
I am the author of the R package [workflowr](https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr), which integrates version control and R Markdown websites. A workflowr user, @Tutuchan, recently reported that the figures are not rendered when hosting a workflowr website with Shiny Server (https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/119). He determined (and I confirmed) that the problem is due to how workflowr saves the figures. To keep the figure files organized, workflowr saves each figure file in the subdirectory `figure/<filename>.Rmd/`. Unfortunately it appears that Shiny Server assumes that the subdirectory is a file since it contains a file extension.

Would it be possible to update Shiny Server to distinguish between files and directories that end with `.Rmd` (potentially [here](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/4b588a12f844713729991d1274764d854d90a18d/lib/router/router.js#L236-L244))? To assist with testing, I put together a minimal example R Markdown file that demonstrates the filepath issue in an [RStudio Cloud project](https://rstudio.cloud/project/60968) (and also copied the R Markdown file below):

````
---
title: "Subdirectory name confused for filename"
date: 2018-08-31
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: false
---

On Shiny Server, using a filename as the name of a subdirectory breaks the
filepath to the figure.

```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "figure/index.Rmd/")
```

This plot does not render.

```{r plot1}
plot(1:10)
```

Removing the file extension from the subdirectory name removes the problem.

```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "figure/index/")
```

This plot renders.

```{r plot2}
hist(rnorm(100))
```
````

title: "enterprise-ready dashboard" drilldown fails mysteriously on shiny server pro
description:
I've implemented a dashboard similar to [this example](https://rviews.rstudio.com/2017/09/20/dashboards-with-r-and-databases); however, the problem reproduces itself using this unmodified [gist.](https://gist.github.com/edgararuiz/89e771b5d1b82adaa0033c0928d1846d)

After two clicks into a highchart object for additional detail, the third click and beyond will only return data from whatever element was clicked second. This is illustrated in the images below (note the dest_name column):

Works as expected:
![first drill](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12927842/41512016-52cc84fa-7250-11e8-9e98-49235bec8687.PNG)

Works as expected:
![second drill](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12927842/41512018-52e1f36c-7250-11e8-8a88-83aa27454a4a.PNG)

The problem does not occur when the app is run locally (from my Windows machine):

I've also deployed a dockerized version of the app (based on the r-base image), and the problem does not appear there either. I think that this is a therefore a shiny-server pro problem, but please move it to the appropriate place if I'm wrong.

Thanks!

title: Trailing slash redirect issue when shiny-server a proxy with a custom path
description:
I follow the directions at https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/213733868-Running-Shiny-Server-with-a-Proxy to serve shiny apps behind a reverse nginx proxy under the `/shiny/` path.

The server is configured to serve apps from user directories.

It mostly works, except in the case that trailing slash is omitted - e.g. `/shiny/username` instead of `/shiny/username/` , shiny attempts to redirect to the path with the trailing slash added but instead redirects to `/username/` (without the base path), which obviously doesn't exist giving a 404 error.

I tried all kinds of settings and suggestions, e.g. adding a nginx rewrite rule to add the trailing slash to the request, but every solution broke something else (asset loading, websockets, etc).

I also tried to change the base location path in the shiny server config to `/shiny/` and then set nginx proxy to direct to `localhost:3838/shiny/`, but the problem persists, suggesting shiny doesn't at all take into account the base path from which it is being served even when this is in its own config rather than the proxy config.

title: Use process.initgroups instead of unixgroups.initgroups
description:
Please switch from [node-unixgroups](https://github.com/jrozner/node-unixgroups) (resp. your fork) to [process.initgroups](https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#process_process_initgroups_user_extra_group) which was added to Node.js in version 0.9.4. node-unixgroup is long dead and the original author suggests to use the corresponding functions from process.* (see https://github.com/jrozner/node-unixgroups/pull/1#issuecomment-381355571)

It only seems to be used in https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/lib/worker/run-as.js#L29

[It would also make the process of upgrading Node.js dependencies easier (see 
[https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Updating-Node.js-package-dependencies](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Updating-Node.js-package-dependencies))]

title: shiny-server - Error getting worker: Error: The application exited during initialization.
description:
I get this with one application running on a local server and not with other applications on the same server. I do not get the shiny window on screen, instead the error appears and nothing further.

> [2018-04-09 20:32:18.789] [INFO] shiny-server - Error getting worker: Error: The application exited during initialization.

The app works well when ran under Studio locally. The input zip is ~50Mb.

I attach the full code of my rather simle app in case someone could point me to the issue

> I run on a 3.10.0-693.el7.x86_64 machine
> R version 3.4.3 (2017-11-30) -- "Kite-Eating Tree"
> Copyright (C) 2017 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
> Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)
> opt/shiny-server/ext/node/bin/shiny-server --version = v6.10.3

Thanks in advance

```
# assemblyNplot.shinyapp
# a Shiny web application that draws N graphs from a zip of denovo assemblies

library("shiny")
library("shinyBS")
library("seqinr")
library("ggplot2")
library("scales")
library("DT")

# you may uncomment the next line to allow large input files (4GB)
options(shiny.maxRequestSize=4*1000*1024^2)
# the following test checks if we are running on shinnyapps.io to limit file size dynamically
# ref: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31423144/how-to-know-if-the-app-is-running-at-local-or-on-server-r-shiny/31425801#31425801
#if ( Sys.getenv('SHINY_PORT') == "" ) { options(shiny.maxRequestSize=1000*1024^2) }

app.name <- "assemblyNplot"
script.version <- "1.0"

# measure sequence lengths from fasta
Fasta2length <-function(fastaFile) {
  #fa <- read.fasta(file = fastaFile, as.string = TRUE, seqonly = TRUE)
  fl <- getLength(read.fasta(file = fastaFile, as.string = TRUE, seqonly = TRUE))
  # return a vector of lengths
  as.vector(fl)
}

# compute XNXX function
Nvalue <- function(lim, x, na.rm = TRUE) {
  # handle NA values
  if(isTRUE(na.rm)){
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
    }
  cutval <- 100/lim
  # compute LXX and NXX
  sorted <- sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)
  SXX <- sum(x)/cutval
  csum <- cumsum(sorted)
  GTLXX <- as.vector(csum >= SXX)
  LXX=min(which(GTLXX == TRUE))
  NXX <- round(sorted[LXX], 1)
  # eg: get NXX with lst['NXX']
  NXX
  }

# format with thousand separator
fnum <- function(x) {
  return(format(as.numeric(x), nsmall=0, big.mark="'"))
}

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(
  HTML('<style type="text/css">
       .row-fluid { width: 25%; }
       .well { background-color: #99CCFF; }
       .shiny-html-output { font-size: 14px; line-height: 15px; }
       </style>'),
  
  # Application header
  headerPanel("Plot N-graphs from a Zip of de-novo assembly fasta files"),
  
  # Application title
  titlePanel(
    windowTitle = "AssemblyNplot",
    tags$a(href="https://corefacilities.vib.be/nc", target="_blank",
           img(src='logo.png', align = "right", width="150", height="58.5", alt="VIB Nucleomics Core"))
    ),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    # show file import and molecule filters
    sidebarPanel(
       tipify(fileInput("upload", "Upload", accept = ".zip"), 
              "A zip files containing all fasta assemblies to plot"),
       br(),
       actionButton("process", "Process uploaded data"),
       hr(),
       textInput('outfile', "name for output File:", value="assemblyNplot"),
       selectInput("format", "Output format (png or pdf):", c("png", "pdf"), selected="pdf"),
       downloadButton('downloadPlot', 'Download Plot')
    ),
  
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput('plot', width = "100%"),
    div(DT::dataTableOutput('ntable'), style = "font-size: 75%; width: 75%")
    )
  )
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {

  fasta.files <- eventReactive({input$process}, {
    unzip.files <- unzip(input$upload$datapath, list = FALSE)
    # get rid of OSX hidden and empty stuff
    fasta.files <- subset(unzip.files, !grepl("__MACOSX|.DS_Store|/$", unzip.files))
    fasta.files
    })
  
  parse.data <- reactive({
    if (is.null(fasta.files())) return(NULL)
    
    # initialize
    n.table <- data.frame()
    n <- length(fasta.files())
    
    withProgress(message = 'Analyzing ', value = 0, {
      for (assembly in fasta.files()){
        title <- basename(assembly)
        incProgress(1/n, detail = title)
        lengths <- Fasta2length(assembly)
        width <- sum(lengths)
        x <- seq(1, 100, by=1)
        y <- sapply(x, function(x) Nvalue(x, lengths))
        name <- rep(title, length(x))
        width <- rep(fnum(width), length(x))
        dat <- data.frame(assembly=paste0(name," (", width,")"), x=x, y=y)
        n.table <- rbind(n.table, dat)
        }
      })
    as.data.frame(n.table)
  })

  output$ntable = DT::renderDataTable({
    if (is.null(parse.data())) return(NULL)
    parse.data()
    })
  
  plotInput <- reactive({
    df <- parse.data()
    # convert to kilobases in plot
    p <- ggplot(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y/1000, group=assembly, colour=assembly)) + 
      scale_y_continuous(trans="log10",labels = waiver()) +
      annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +
      geom_line(size = 0.75, linetype="dotted") + 
      geom_point(aes(shape=assembly), size = 2) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype="dotted", 
                 color = "red", size=0.5) +
      ggtitle("NG graphs of the assemblies in scaffold length") + 
      labs(x = "NG%", y = "Contig/Scaffold length (kb)") +
      labs(x = "NG", y = "Scaffold NG length (kb)") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour="grey20",size=8,angle=0,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="plain"),
            axis.text.y = element_text(colour="grey20",size=8,angle=0,hjust=1,vjust=0,face="plain"),
            axis.title.x = element_text(colour="grey20",size=10,angle=0,hjust=.5,vjust=0,face="plain"),
            axis.title.y = element_text(colour="grey20",size=10,angle=90,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="plain"),
            legend.justification = c(0,1),
            legend.position = c(0.1,0.5),
            legend.title = element_blank(),
            legend.text = element_text(size=10),
            legend.key = element_rect(colour = NA, fill = NA),
            legend.key.size = unit(0.8, 'lines'),
            legend.background = element_rect(fill="transparent"),
            plot.title = element_text(margin=margin(b=0), size = 16))
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    plot(plotInput(), width="640px", height="480px")
  })
  
  output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() { paste(input$outfile, input$format, sep=".") },
    content = function(file) {
      if(input$format == "png")
        png(file, width = 640, height = 480, units = "px") # open the png device
      else
        pdf(file, width = 8, height = 6) # open the pdf device
      plot(plotInput())
      dev.off()  # turn the device off
    }
  )
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

    && cd shiny-server \ 
    && DIR=`pwd`  \
    && PATH=$DIR/bin:$PATH \
    && mkdir tmp \ 
    && cd tmp \ 
    && PYTHON=`which python` \
    && ../packaging/make-package.sh\

RUN ln -s /usr/local/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server /usr/bin/shiny-server \

RUN mkdir /srv/shiny-server/example \

EXPOSE 3838

COPY shiny-server.sh /usr/bin/shiny-server.sh

CMD ["/usr/bin/shiny-server.sh"]

title: URL processing for session$clientData$url_pathname
description:
As shinyapps.io and other Shiny Servers are configured, the session$clientData$url_pathname reactive will never return anything but "/". This is because the server will return a Not Found error on longer URLs. Rather than 404 out, the server should redirect these paths back to the app, with the full path in session$clientData$url_pathname.

For Apache servers, the required setting is discussed in the **Fallback Resource** section of this page of the manual: http://httpd.apache.org/docs/current/rewrite/remapping.html. 

Being able to get the path would allow the creation of URL-based, multi-page reactive Shiny web sites. There's a demo of how to do this using the URL "search" protocol at https://open-meta.shinyapps.io/uistub/. The code is at https://github.com/open-meta/uiStub.

(The shiny server is on port 8080, my main app is on 80)

In shiny, I serve the HTML content from `static/` like so:

```R
addResourcePath('static', directory_containing_foo_html)

title: server launcher builds but does not run on FreeBSD
description:
Currently it errors out looking for something in /proc

FreeBSD supports "linprocfs" which allows for linux /proc support.
When the FreeBSD linuxulator is setup to provide a linux userland environment, the path is usually /compat/linux/proc, so if you test for /compat/linux your launcher can function without modification (I tested this).

When I dug into the code it looks like y'all are attempting to determine the path of the executable in a non-portable way.  In looking for the simplest solution, it appears that Boost offers a favorably licensed way of dealing with this should you decide to change.

title: Shiny server with user_dirs breaks DT datatables that start with a "."
description:
Odd little corner case here. I have installed "shinyURL" to create a shortcut link to a specific input of my Rmd site. On that page is a shiny datatable widget. It functions fine in rstudio, but failed when I copied the code to the "server" location, which is running with shiny studio open source, with "user_dirs" configuration enabled. The error was an AJAX error from DT (https://datatables.net/manual/tech-notes/7). Inspecting the network traffic from browser to shiny server, it appears that there is a 403 error being returned by the "server data" component behind DT. There is no error in the shiny log files, so it looks like shiny-server itself is responsible.

```
dataTableOutput(".activitytable")
output$.activitytable <- renderDataTable({
  myactivity() %>% arrange(desc(date)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(date=strftime(date, format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), `Error Rate`=sprintf(`Error Rate` * 100, fmt="%.2f%%"))
}, options = list(
 columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 5))
) )
```

Renaming the datatable in the output (to .activitytable) is the immediate cause - this is done so the shinyURL addon doesn't encode the datatable state in the URL (which is unnecessary in my application).

The URL being requested of shiny-server is `<server>/session/<hash>/dataobj/.activitytable?w=&nonce=<nonce>` from DT. With a user-dirs configuration, the fetch of this URL is returning HTTP 403 (Forbidden) with an html response page containing "Forbidden".

I reconfigured my server to remove the "user-dirs" configuration command and host *the exact same code* using app_dir/log_dir instead, and it now works.

title: Sanitizing error messages
description: I just spent quite a bit of time debugging some issues with a shiny app after I decided to update my shiny server. I kept getting the same error over and over; `An error has occurred. Check your logs or contact the app author for clarification.` After looking a bit at the documentation and understanding a little more about sanitizing errors I decided to add `sanitize_errors false;` to the config file. title: No Grey Screen with Reconnect Disabled
description:
With a global config setting `reconnect false;`, open a Shiny app and then kill the server. You are not notified of the disconnection in any way.

After looking at the `shiny-server-client` code, it looks like the new `reconnect` decorator is emitting the “disconnect” event that `main.js` uses to determine when the connection goes down. However, this decorator isn’t even used if reconnect is disabled, hence the lack of disconnect notification when reconnect is not enabled.

I’m a bit unclear on how to approach fixing it without a bit of guidance. @jcheng5 or @trestletech, ping me if you have any suggestions.

title: 204 No Content error on Apache shiny server when client is busy rendering webpage
description:
Hi,

When shiny apps are running behind a proxy with Apache, and the client performance is poor (freeze tens of seconds while rendering the webpage), client is disconnected with a 204 error on Apache logs:

`mod_dumpio.c(103): [client vv.xx.yy.zz:aaaaaaa] mod_dumpio:  dumpio_out (data-HEAP): HTTP/1.1 204 No Content\r\nDate: Thu, 02 Jun 2016 14:37:28 GMT\r\nServer: Apache/2.4.18 (Unix)\r\nCache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0\r\nAccess-Control-Allow-Origin: http://www.example.com\r\nVary: Origin\r\nAccess-Control-Allow-Credentials: true\r\nContent-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nKeep-Alive: timeout=120, max=99\r\nConnection: Keep-Alive\r\n\r\n`

This does never happens if the App is run locally or runs in shinyapps.io. Same computer is perfectly able to render the webpage without disconnecting.

A minimalistic App to trigger the disconnection:
[https://gist.github.com/gdevailly/cb12cf3d8920020117d914714083a802](https://gist.github.com/gdevailly/cb12cf3d8920020117d914714083a802)

The **go** button while fill the selectInput with as many random value as the slider specify.
It works fine until a point, very dependent on the client performance.
On my crappy laptop, around 15.000 values, the browser freeze a bit and is then disconnected from the Apache server with a code 204 (grey veil on the app), right after rendering the selectInput.

I am not sure if its a bug, a feature, or an issue with our Apache config, but this is quite annoying for client with poor performance browsers.

Any suggestion welcome,

Guillaume

title: RODBC Connection Brings Down Shiny Server
description:
We've been struggling with this nasty issue for a while, and I'm pretty certain it's a bug in the server.

**Environment**:
- OS - RedHat 6.7
- Shiny Version - 0.12.2

**Summary**:
If there is an RODBC connection in the Shiny Server code, then a segfault will be generated.

**Reproducer**:
1. Create a shiny app and add an RODBC connection that queries a database.
2. View the app and you should get a traceback.

There are more details as well as a stack trace in the following links.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/34316243/rodbc-query-brings-down-shiny-server
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/66Ve60ugmHs

title: Failing to start ShinyServer - PIDFile issue?
description:
I'm experiencing problems starting up my Shiny server on RHEL 7. Weirdly enough everything worked smoothly until I had to restart my machine. Now every attempt to start Shiny server produces this:

```
]# sudo systemctl start shiny-server
Job for shiny-server.service failed. See 'systemctl status shiny-server.service' and 'journalctl -xn' for details.
]# systemctl status shiny-server -l
shiny-server.service - ShinyServer
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service; enabled)
   Active: failed (Result: timeout) since Mi 2015-12-09 11:48:52 CET; 4s ago
  Process: 7686 ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/sleep 5 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
  Process: 7675 ExecStart=/usr/bin/bash -c /opt/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server --pidfile=/var/run/shiny-server/shiny-server.pid >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
 Main PID: 7675 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)

Dez 09 11:48:47 vf-urmo.intra.dlr.de systemd[1]: shiny-server.service operation timed out. Stopping.
Dez 09 11:48:52 vf-urmo.intra.dlr.de systemd[1]: Failed to start ShinyServer.
Dez 09 11:48:52 vf-urmo.intra.dlr.de systemd[1]: Unit shiny-server.service entered failed state.
```

I already tried modifying `/etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service` so that it should write its PID file in a subfolder of `/var/run` (by tweaking the `--pidfile` parameter to `ExecStart` as well as the `PIDFile=` parameter, and adding `User=shiny` to ensure user `shiny` is actually trying to write any PID files) but that didn't solve the issue either:

```
[Unit]
Description=ShinyServer

[Service]
TimeoutStartSec=10
ExecStart=/usr/bin/bash -c '/opt/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server --pidfile=/var/run/shiny-server/shiny-server.pid >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1'
# Needed to give SS a chance to write out to the PID file.
ExecStartPost=/usr/bin/sleep 3
PIDFile=/var/run/shiny-server/shiny-server.pid
Type=simple
User=shiny

ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/sleep 5
RestartSec=1

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

I restarted the daemon after these edits:

```
]# sudo systemctl daemon-reload
```

Needless to say I made sure user `shiny` has write permissions in the subfolder mentioned above:

```
]# mkdir /var/run/shiny-server/
]# chown shiny:shiny /var/run/shiny-server/
```

title: "running as root unnecessarily" despite config
description:
**Summary**

I think the config file says to run as a specific user, but the logs (et al) report running as root.

Similar perhaps to #153, but that seems to be more address-in-use though it also shows this problem.

**Expected**

Based on the config file (below), I would expect `ps` to report the owning user as "shiny".

**Actual**

The logfile, `ps`, and `netstat` all report the process running as root.

**Context**

Installed on a clean Ubuntu 14.04.3 amd64 (server), shiny-server-1.4.1.759. I believe it's a standard install, direct, nothing changed. The user "shiny" is in the passwd file, and root can `su shiny` without problem. Nothing in the home directory has been altered, and the three files (`.bash_logout`, `.bashrc`, `.profile`) are straight copies from `/etc/skel/`. There are no other log entries indicating other errors.

This is a relatively-stock ubuntu server, very little personalized. I appreciate any guidance you can offer, sorry if this is a repeat to something I didn't find.

`$ cat /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf`

```
# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;
# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;
  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {
    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}
```

`$ tail -5 /var/log/shiny-server.log`

title: Add try/catch around process.kill calls
description: app-worker.js calls process.kill, both of these calls need try/catch around them. If sending SIGINT fails, there's no need to do anything else (i.e. don't do the SIGKILL). If either fails with ESRCH we shouldn't even log it. (Or maybe just never log.)

description:
I've just posted the following issue on stackoverflow. Any help is welcome

I have created two dockers with shiny server on `centos`:
- Docker with `shiny server` - free edition [here](https://github.com/smartinsightsfromdata/Docker-for-shiny-server-free-edition-on-centos)
- Docker with `shiny server pro` (using a temporary license) [here](https://github.com/smartinsightsfromdata/Docker-shiny-server-pro-on-centos)

These dockers are on `centos`, as it is assumed eventually will run on `RHEL` as a supported version of Linux (maybe dockerised or native). For the time being they offer a convenient way for testing and development.

They are mainly designed for development: they include `R`, `RStudio Server` and `Shiny Server`: probably not what a Docker purist would do or recommend (probably a production version will be based on docker compose).

The problem I have is that while the Docker with `shiny server` - free edition works fine, **the Docker with `shiny server pro` does not work** (maybe an issue with supervisord?). 

This is quite surprising as the code base is common (of course).  Maybe an issue on how the processes are spawn?

It would be great if somebody would help me to find the bug in the `shiny server pro` config.

title: shiny-server to follow symbolic links?
description:
Is there any directive to permit shiny-server to follow symbolic links?
Example (desired) use case:

```
+---/myApp
    +---server.R
    +---ui.R
    +---www
        +---some_plugin.js -> ../lib/some_plugin_v1/the_plugin_code.js
    +---lib
        +---some_plugin_v1
            +---the_plugin_code.js
    +---lib
        +---some_plugin_v2
            +---the_plugin_code.js
```

In the current world, it appears the symlink under `www` isn't followed, so swapping between versions of the plugin require copying the file to the `www` location.

Tangentially related: it seems that server-level apps use `assets` as the subdirectory in which to find additional files, but for user-level apps it's `www`... is this distinction intentional?
(It's easy enough to rename the directories when migrating user-level apps to server-level and vice-versa, but it's not documented in the current shiny-server configuration guide, so might be worth a documentation addition.)

title: <base> tag interferes with svg rendering
description:
(I don't know that this is necessarily a problem to be fixed in Shiny Server itself, but I thought I'd file it here anyway.)

SVG gradients don't display properly when they're in a Shiny app accessed through Shiny Server. This is a problem for ggvis: rstudio/ggvis#236.

The root of the problem is that, in SVGs, gradients are defined and referenced this way, and it's affected by the `<base>` tag:

```
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="foo" ...>...</linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect fill="url(#foo)" ... />
```

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7759371/svg-gradient-turns-black-when-there-is-a-base-tag-in-html-page

title: Crockford's json2.js for IE8
description:
I created an app containing multi-byte characters yesterday: https://demo.shinyapps.io/022-unicode-chinese/ It works well on most web browsers except IE8, in which `JSON.stringify()` seems to be encoding messages using the `\uxxxx` representation for multi-byte Unicode characters, leading to difficulties in `RJSONIO::fromJSON()` when decoding the messages.

One solution that @jcheng5 found was to use Crockford's json2.js (https://github.com/douglascrockford/JSON-js). I re-deployed the app after including json2.js in the app: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/commit/1cfa8350167acc443f31e0a13740eaad02d3428f Now IE8 works well, so perhaps Shiny Server should just include this json2.js for IE8.

There is a minor issue when opening that app in IE8: there is a warning about the https connection, which I do not quite understand.

title: Server-side updateSelectizeInput fails when server is restarted
description:
Thank you very much for the recent addition of the server-side implementation of updateSelectizeInput(). This has proven very useful for my application!

Unfortunately, the method starts failing when the server is restart during an active session of the app. I am surprised because the other components of shiny remaining unaffected by a server-side restart. Here is a simple illustration:

ui.R

```
library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage( 
    actionButton("restart","Restart"),
    selectizeInput("city",
          "City name:", choices=NULL,multiple=F, options=list(placeholder="Type Tokyo")),
    plotOutput("cityPlot")
))
```

server.R

```
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {  
    updateSelectizeInput(session,"city",choices=c("New York","Sydney","London","Tokyo"),server=TRUE)
    output$cityPlot<- renderPlot({
        if(input$restart) {
            message("restart")
            write.table(c(),file="restart.txt")
        }
        })
})
```

Load the app in shiny-server and begin to type "Tokyo" in the selectizeInput. You will see a list of dropdowns appearing.
Now, manually reload the webpage. Push the "Restart" button in the app. Try to type "Tokyo" in the selectizeInput. No dropdowns will appear.

Thanks!

-Winn

description:
Hi folks,

Was not sure what's the best place to submit this - please move where appropriate.

I have a question and wonder if you have come across this.

Hypothetically an app exceeds its specified init timeout (App is somehow ill-designed and [R] process is stuck spinning away).

Looks like the scheduler will give up trying to get a handle on the worker, and the user will get a nice

Am I missing something in the process flow?

Thanks

title: [wiki] Ubuntu installation instructions wrong, triggering bash syntax errors.
description:
There is an incorrect command in the Wiki page for how to install this software on Ubuntu.

This link has the instructions: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Ubuntu-step-by-step-install-instructions

The instructions use this as one of the commands to run: `sudo su - -c "R -e \\"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\\""`.

It incorrectly escapes the quote, because `\\"` is interpreted as an escaped `\` character followed by a Bash-interpreted `"` character which means Bash sees `sudo su - -c "R -e \"` as the command it has to deal with, which triggers a syntax error with everything after that.

To fix this, the command in the instructions needs to be changed to this: `sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""`

The modified command correctly escapes the quotes, which will prevent individuals from getting syntax errors on that command in the install guide.

( This was addressed in this question on Ask Ubuntu: http://askubuntu.com/questions/382232/when-trying-to-install-shiny-server-for-r-on-ubuntu-12-04-the-command-in-the-se )

title: Building Shiny Server from Source directions have invalid cmake command
description:
The [Building Shiny Server from Source](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Building-Shiny-Server-from-Source) page in the wiki contains an invalid cmake command:

```
cmake --DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local -DPYTHON="$PYTHON" ../
```

When I attempt to change the value of CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX usign this syntax, CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX is not honored---it still attempts to install into the default /usr/local. Using only one hyphen in front of "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX" instead of two fixed this; i.e.:

```
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local -DPYTHON="$PYTHON" ../
```

title: shiny server upstart init script - server doesn't start on boot
description:
Following the Ubuntu 13.04 shiny server install wiki, for me the upstart init script doesn't start shiny server on boot.  I changed "start on stopped networking" to "start on started networking" and now shiny server starts on boot.

This issue has happened on two separate installs for me; one on a desktop 13.04 install and one a server 13.04 install on a VPS.  Please let me know if you can replicate this behavior.

description:

title: Cache Supplemented AppSpec in config-router
description:
There's no reason to hit the disk to check for local .shiny_app.conf files on every request. These should be cached in a hash as follows:

```
[original appSpec] --> [enhancedAppSpec]
```

Note that we'll want a way to prevent these from accumulating over the lifetime of the server. At the very least, we should be able to wipe out the ones that haven't been recently used. Realistically, we should probably have a scheduler kill itself and emit an event when it has no more workers.
